questions.title: What attaches to the superior temporal line
questions.question: Which of the following anatomical structures is specifically attached to the superior temporal line of the skull?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The temporalis muscle itself attaches lower down, at the inferior temporal line, not the superior temporal line.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The masseter muscle attaches to the zygomatic arch and the angle and ramus of the mandible, nowhere near the superior temporal line.
explanations.C: Correct. The temporalis muscle occupies the temporal fossa and is covered by a tough sheet of deep fascia, the temporal fascia, which attaches above to the superior temporal line and splits into two layers near the zygomatic arch. The muscle itself takes origin lower, at the inferior temporal line, so the fascia and the muscle it covers attach at two different lines only a short distance apart.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The zygomatic arch is where the temporal fascia's two layers insert below, not where the superior temporal line attachment described in the question sits.

questions.learning_objective: State that the temporal fascia, not the temporalis muscle, attaches to the superior temporal line.
